turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Youre making a mistake, tough guy. Whoever he is, your guys not one of Friedmans...

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: You really are a piece of work, you know that? You walk out on me and my family for some worthless bum and you expect us to help him when he screws up.

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: You need to come down here, everybody meets everybody. Ho ho ho. Ha ha ha. We do one for good faith and then we talk about airplanes.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: But you must. It's the only way.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: I just got released five minutes ago.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: George, are we gonna do this or not?

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: I don't suppose there's a drink left...

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: You can have one at Max's.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: I don't think I'm going.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Why not?

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Because I don't want to.

turns.text: Max has gone to a great deal of trouble, it's going to be an elaborate party, and it's for you.

turns.text: No, it's not. It's for this.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: It's the same thing, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: You're being childish.

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: May I lift my eyebrows? What is this? What are you trying to do?

turns.text: I'm trying to get Susie to stand up to you. But your manner is so threatening that she's afraid to speak!

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Son, you raise your voice again and you'll be outa here on your golden pratt!

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: How come you don't hate their guts?

turns.text: I don't know. I guess I'm not afraid of them.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: You were plenty scared that night in the car.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Just of getting hurt. They can't touch me inside.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Like hell they can't. They can reach right in with their damn white hands and turn you off and on.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Not if you see them for what they are, Duff.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Jesus, baby, you're so full of talk! Well, you ain't never really been a nigger, have you - livin' like that in your father's house! So just shut your mouth.

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: He didn't mean it. You know Johnny. He's always been a hothead --

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: It's not him. It's them. I can't live like this.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Just give Reed a little more time. You know how he works -- analyzing every little step before he takes one --

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: It's easy for you to be patient.

turns.speaker: Person1

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: It's so beautiful ... and sad.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Sad?

turns.text: Lost. it feels lost. This was hers?

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Yeah ... well, yours. You still don't believe that you're the Princess, do you?

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: I know I must have had something to do with the palace - I've had little flashes of things - but being the Princess? It doesn't matter as long as I find my home.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Well, the only thing you've got when you've got a home is a fear of losing it! You're lucky you don't remember the revolution -- I never had much, but what I did have -- I lost.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: I'm sorry.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Hey! It doesn't matter! You gotta make your own way in the world! Don't be sorry for me! I'm going to get what I want don't you worry!

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Well... come on.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: This is a mistake. No. This is a disaster.

turns.speaker: Person1
turns.text: Come on, it's just what you need! Let everyone see you. Talk to them, live it up!

turns.text: Why not?

turns.text: He called the day he escaped.

turns.text: He said he wished the two of you could start over, live a normal life.

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: Huh. Problem is, Jack's idea of a normal life is robbing banks. It's all he's ever done.

turns.text: Did you know that when you married him?

turns.speaker: Person2
turns.text: He said he was a card player. I could live with that. I never knew he robbed banks till he got busted with that car that caught fire -- if you can imagine something like that happening, comes out of the bank and the car's on fire. I did go see him in jail to tell him I was filing for divorce. He said, "Okay." Jack's so easy going. He was fun, but never what you'd call a real husband.

dialogues.label_scope: whole dialogue; not localised to any turn

turns.text: I was grieving too.

turns.text: So what are you saying?

turns.text: I'm saying now you do know. So it's time for you to move on.

turns.text: You left her. How's that for a fact?

turns.text: How's this for a fact? I loved her first.
